function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.

**How Turbonomic Helps Unilever Leverage AI for Multi‑Cloud Observability**

| Aspect | What Turbonomic Brings | Why It Matters for Unilever |
|--------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| **Unified Visibility** | Aggregates real‑time telemetry from all workloads—VMs, containers, serverless functions, databases, etc.—across on‑prem, GCP, AWS, Azure, and other clouds into a single pane. | Unilever can see the entire application stack without switching dashboards or pulling logs from disparate sources. |
| **Intelligent Resource Allocation** | Uses machine learning to predict demand spikes, capacity gaps, and performance bottlenecks, then automatically recommends or enacts right‑size moves (scale‑up/down, move-to‑cloud, pause/stop). | Reduces over‑provisioning costs while ensuring critical consumer‑facing services stay responsive during seasonal peaks. |
| **Policy‑Based Automation** | Lets Unilever define business‑driven policies (e.g., “Keep e‑commerce latency < 200 ms” or “Do not exceed $X/month on cloud spend”). Turbonomic continuously checks compliance and triggers remediation actions. | Aligns IT operations with corporate sustainability goals and cost‑control mandates. |
| **Cost Optimization & Forecasting** | Provides day‑to‑day cost attribution per workload, predicts future spend, and offers actionable recommendations (e.g., “Move this container to a lower‑tier instance type”). | Enables Unilever’s finance team to forecast budgets accurately and identify savings opportunities before they hit the bill. |
| **Cross‑Cloud Workload Mobility** | Detects when a workload would benefit from moving to another provider (or back to on‑prem) based on performance, cost, or regulatory constraints, and orchestrates the migration with minimal downtime. | Gives Unilever flexibility to avoid vendor lock‑in and to take advantage of region‑specific pricing or compliance features. |
| **Observability & Root‑Cause Analysis** | Correlates metrics, logs, and traces across clouds to surface root causes of performance issues, even when they span multiple providers. | Accelerates incident response and reduces mean time to resolution (MTTR) for global supply‑chain applications. |

---

### Difference Between Turbonomic and Native Cloud Observability Tools

| Feature | Turbonomic | GCP Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver) | AWS CloudWatch | Azure Monitor |
|---------|------------|-------------------------------------------|----------------|---------------|
| **Scope** | Cross‑cloud + on‑prem | Cloud‑native only | Cloud‑native only | Cloud‑native only |
| **Data Sources** | VMs, containers, Kubernetes, serverless, databases, storage, networking, hypervisors, SaaS APIs | Cloud‑native metrics, logs, traces | Cloud‑native metrics, logs, traces | Cloud‑native metrics, logs, traces |
| **AI/ML Capabilities** | Predictive analytics, automated remediation, policy enforcement | Basic anomaly detection, alerting | Basic anomaly detection, alerting | Basic anomaly detection, alerting |
| **Automation** | Policy‑driven auto‑remediation, auto‑migration, auto‑right‑sizing | Manual scaling via Cloud Functions or automation scripts | Manual scaling via Lambda or automation scripts | Manual scaling via Logic Apps or automation scripts |
| **Cost Attribution** | Detailed cost breakdown per workload, forecast, optimization recommendations | Cost Explorer provides high‑level cost views | Cost Explorer provides high‑level cost views | Cost Management provides high‑level cost views |
| **Multi‑Cloud Governance** | Unified policy engine that spans all providers | Provider‑specific policies only | Provider‑specific policies only | Provider‑specific policies only |
| **Root‑Cause Analysis** | Correlates events across clouds, provides actionable insights | Cloud‑native RCA limited to provider | Cloud‑native RCA limited to provider | Cloud‑native RCA limited to provider |
| **Ease of Adoption** | One console, one set of APIs, one learning curve | Separate consoles/APIs per provider | Separate consoles/APIs per provider | Separate consoles/APIs per provider |

**Bottom Line:**  
Turbonomic acts as a *single, AI‑powered control plane* that sits above the native observability stacks of GCP, AWS, and Azure. While each cloud’s native tools excel at monitoring within their own ecosystem, Turbonomic brings cross‑cloud intelligence, automated decision‑making, and unified cost governance—exactly what Unilever needs to manage its global, hybrid‑cloud footprint efficiently and sustainably.
